subject: ScalePath renewal: operational scale and GPU addition scenarios
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Darren Wu <darren.wu@scalepath.io>, Priya Menon <priya.m@scalepath.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ScalePath renewal — operational scale + GPU addition scenarios

Hi Darren / Priya,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I put together three pragmatic scenarios for your renewal that map current utilization to committed GPU lanes. The attached capacity matrix summarizes recent 90-day peak windows, average concurrency, and inferred slot utilization based on token throughput.

Quick summary (see attachment for numbers):
- Scenario A (Conservative): +0 GPUs, keep current commit, add 15% burst credit. Best for teams prioritizing cost predictability.
- Scenario B (Balanced): +8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved. Targets 85% steady-state utilization with a small dedicated burst pool; expected 12% lower per-token cost versus A.
- Scenario C (Aggressive): +20 GPUs reserved for peak smoothing and faster latency SLOs. Higher monthly spend but reduces queuing events for tail traffic.

Ask: Can you confirm which scenario aligns with (a) your Q3 product launch throughput target and (b) the procurement timeline? If helpful, we can run a model where we convert a portion of your existing burst usage into a smaller reserved tranche to preserve headroom while lowering unit costs.

Attachments: [Attachment: scalepath_capacity_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the matrix tomorrow.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Darren Wu <darren.wu@scalepath.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@scalepath.io>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: ScalePath renewal — operational scale + GPU addition scenarios

Rafael — thanks for the breakdown and the attachment. Priya and I reviewed the matrix with engineering. A few notes:

- We have a major customer pilot launching mid-July that could double peak concurrency for ~6 weeks. That pilot is the primary driver for wanting more predictable capacity.
- Our infra team prefers minimizing reserved headroom; they asked whether we can keep target utilization at ~90% and still preserve a small burst pool for sudden spikes.
- Pricing sensitivity: Procurement will push back on any >15% increase in run-rate without a clearer freight/fallback plan.

Specific question: For Scenario B, can Redwood provide an automated fallback policy that routes low-priority traffic to the burst pool and preserves reserved GPUs for critical inference? If so, we might be able to justify the +8. Also please share a draft SOW we can send to procurement.

— Darren
Darren Wu
CTO, ScalePath
darren.wu@scalepath.io

Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ScalePath renewal — operational scale + GPU addition scenarios

Rafael — quick internal notes before we send SOW:

- Fallback routing: we can implement a two-tier policy. Reserved tranche handles high-priority inferencing; low-priority jobs are tagged and routed to a shared burst pool. That preserves latency for critical traffic and reduces wasted reserved capacity. Ops can instrument token-level routing and a token budget per request class.
- Pricing: propose a blended rate for Scenario B (8 GPUs) with a 3-month ramp discount (10% off for months 1–3) to ease procurement concerns. Leaves runway for the July pilot.
- SOW: I'll draft a targeted SOW that includes: milestone-based acceptance for pilot, rollback conditions, and an observable runbook for utilization thresholds that trigger temporary autoscale.

I'll attach the SOW draft and a short operational runbook — Rafael, want me to send both to Darren directly or do you want to review first?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Darren Wu <darren.wu@scalepath.io>, Priya Menon <priya.m@scalepath.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ScalePath renewal — operational scale + GPU addition scenarios

Darren / Priya — looping back with the SOW and a practical operational plan attached. Highlights:

1) Scenario B (recommended): +8 reserved GPUs, 10% ramp discount months 1–3, burst pool sized at 20% of peak observed 90-day window.
2) Fallback & routing: two-tier routing enabled by default. Low-priority requests marked client-side (header: X-Redwood-Priority: low) will be queued to the burst pool; critical requests keep reserved lanes.
3) Acceptance: pilot acceptance defined by <1% tail latency degradation during 7-day rolling window. If violation >3 days, automatic temporary top-up credits will be applied and we’ll schedule a capacity review.

Attachments: [Attachment: SOW-ScalePath-GPU-addition-v1.docx] [Attachment: scalepath_capacity_matrix.xlsx]

Next steps: can you confirm procurement timeline (target date to have a signed SOW) and whether you want us to add a clause for a mid-cycle top-up option if the July pilot grows faster than expected? If yes, we’ll include a capped top-up provision in the SOW.

If it helps, I can schedule a 20-min call tomorrow with Ben + Kimberly to walk procurement through the blended pricing and the operational safeguards.

Best — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
